oauth.flowTypeTooltip: Choose how the proxy authenticates with this MCP server. M2M is for server-to-server communication using client credentials. Interactive (PKCE) is for user-facing flows that require browser-based authorization.
oauth.resourceIndicatorTooltip: RFC 8707 resource indicator sent to the authorization server so it mints a token audienced for this MCP server. Leave blank to send nothing, which is the default and what most providers expect. Use 'auto' to send this server's own URL. Set an exact identifier when the authorization server expects a specific one. Some providers reject this parameter and take the audience from scopes instead; if you see AADSTS901002, leave it blank. If you see invalid_target, the authorization server needs it set.
oauth.m2mClientIdTooltip: OAuth2 client ID for the client_credentials grant.
oauth.m2mClientSecretTooltip: OAuth2 client secret for the client_credentials grant.
oauth.m2mTokenUrlTooltip: Token endpoint URL for the client_credentials grant.
oauth.m2mScopesTooltip: Optional scopes to request with the client_credentials grant.
oauth.m2mClientIdRequired: Client ID is required for M2M OAuth
oauth.m2mClientSecretRequired: Client Secret is required for M2M OAuth
oauth.m2mTokenUrlRequired: Token URL is required for M2M OAuth
oauth.interactiveClientIdTooltip: Provide only if your MCP server cannot handle dynamic client registration.
oauth.interactiveScopesTooltip: Optional scopes requested during token exchange. Separate multiple scopes with enter or commas.
oauth.issuerTooltip: OAuth 2.0 authorization server issuer (RFC 8414). Leave empty to discover endpoints from the upstream resource; set it to pin the trust anchor, which makes this issuer's document the only endpoint source (RFC 8414 §3.3), overriding the Authorization/Token/Registration URLs above and failing closed if its metadata cannot be fetched.
oauth.authorizationUrlTooltip: Optional override for the authorization endpoint.
oauth.tokenUrlTooltip: Optional override for the token endpoint.
oauth.registrationUrlTooltip: Optional override for the dynamic client registration endpoint.
oauth.tokenValidationTooltip: JSON object of key-value rules checked against the OAuth token response before storing. Supports dot-notation for nested fields (e.g. {"organization": "my-org", "team.id": "123"}). Tokens that fail validation are rejected with HTTP 403.
oauth.tokenStorageTtlTooltip: How long to cache each user's OAuth access token in Redis before evicting it (never longer than the token's own expires_in). Leave blank to derive the TTL from the token's expires_in, or fall back to the 12-hour default.
oauth.authorizeIntro: Use OAuth to fetch a fresh access token and temporarily save it in the session as the authentication value.

idJag.orgTokenEndpointTooltip: Your IdP org authorization server's token endpoint. LiteLLM exchanges the user's identity assertion here for an ID-JAG assertion (RFC 8693 with requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id-jag).
idJag.orgTokenEndpointRequired: The org token endpoint is required for ID-JAG
idJag.resourceTokenEndpointTooltip: The upstream resource authorization server's token endpoint. LiteLLM posts the ID-JAG assertion here as an RFC 7523 jwt-bearer grant to get the access token the MCP server accepts.
idJag.resourceTokenEndpointRequired: The resource token endpoint is required for ID-JAG
idJag.clientIdTooltip: OAuth2 client ID LiteLLM authenticates as on both legs.
idJag.clientIdRequired: Client ID is required for ID-JAG
idJag.clientSecretTooltip: Authenticates LiteLLM as the OAuth client via client_secret_post. Leave blank when using a private key instead; a private key takes precedence over this secret.
idJag.secretOrPrivateKey: Provide either a client secret or a client private key
idJag.privateKeyTooltip: PEM private key signing the RFC 7523 private_key_jwt client assertion. Okta Cross App Access normally requires this. When set it takes precedence over the client secret.
idJag.privateKeyPlaceholderEdit: -----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY----- (leave blank to keep existing)
idJag.privateKeyIdTooltip: The kid advertised in the client assertion JWT header, so the IdP can select the right registered key.
idJag.signingAlgTooltip: Algorithm signing the client assertion JWT. Defaults to RS256.
idJag.audienceTooltip: RFC 8693 audience sent on leg 1, identifying the upstream the ID-JAG assertion is minted for.
idJag.resourceIndicatorTooltip: RFC 8707 resource indicator sent on leg 1. Separate from Audience, which is the RFC 8693 parameter.
idJag.subjectTokenTypeTooltip: Type of the identity assertion exchanged on leg 1. Defaults to urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token.
idJag.scopesTooltip: Scopes requested on leg 1 of the exchange.

tokenExchange.profileTooltip: Token-exchange wire dialect. RFC 8693 is the standard token-exchange grant. Microsoft Entra OBO uses Entra's On-Behalf-Of dialect (the RFC 7523 jwt-bearer grant with requested_token_use=on_behalf_of) and carries the target resource in a scope like api://<app-id>/.default.
tokenExchange.endpointTooltip: RFC 8693 token endpoint. The proxy exchanges the user's incoming token here for a scoped token used to call the upstream MCP server. Leave blank to auto-discover it from the upstream's protected-resource metadata (RFC 9728 then RFC 8414).
tokenExchange.clientIdTooltip: OAuth2 client ID used to authenticate to the token exchange endpoint.
tokenExchange.clientSecretTooltip: OAuth2 client secret used to authenticate to the token exchange endpoint.
tokenExchange.clientIdRequired: Client ID is required for token exchange
tokenExchange.clientSecretRequired: Client Secret is required for token exchange
tokenExchange.audienceTooltip: Target audience for the exchanged token (RFC 8693 audience). Identifies the upstream MCP server the token is for.
tokenExchange.subjectTokenTypeTooltip: Type of the user's incoming token (RFC 8693 subject_token_type). Defaults to urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token.
tokenExchange.scopesTooltip: Optional scopes to request during the token exchange.
tokenExchange.scopesTooltipEntraObo: Microsoft Entra OBO carries the target resource in the scope, so at least one is required (e.g. api://<app-id>/.default).
tokenExchange.scopesRequired: Microsoft Entra OBO requires a scope, e.g. api://<app-id>/.default

tokenEndpointAuthMethod.label: Token Endpoint Auth Method (optional)
tokenEndpointAuthMethod.tooltip: How the proxy authenticates to the upstream OAuth token endpoint. Client Secret Basic sends the client credentials in an HTTP Basic Authorization header; leave blank to use the default, Client Secret Post, which sends them in the request body.

passthrough.clientIdPlaceholderKeep: Leave blank to keep the currently saved app (if any)
passthrough.clientIdPlaceholderDcr: Leave blank to use dynamic client registration
passthrough.clientSecretPlaceholderKeep: Leave blank to keep the currently saved secret (if any)
passthrough.clientSecretPlaceholderPkce: Leave blank for public clients / PKCE
passthrough.clientIdHelpKeep: Set this to make everyone authorize through a specific app; required for upstreams without dynamic client registration (e.g. a pre-registered Slack app).
passthrough.clientIdHelpDcr: Switching the auth type discards the previously saved app; enter a client ID here or leave blank to use dynamic client registration.
passthrough.intro: Callers bring their own upstream token for this auth type, so LiteLLM never stores tokens. To preview tools and configure the tool allowlist, authorize against the upstream here: the token stays in this browser session only and is never saved to LiteLLM. An OAuth app configured below IS saved with the server, so internal users who authorize from the Tools page go through it.
passthrough.upstreamChanged: You changed the upstream URL or endpoints; the OAuth app entered here was registered for the previous upstream and may not be valid. Update the client ID, or clear it to use dynamic client registration.
passthrough.removeSavedApp: Remove the saved OAuth app on save (the server goes back to dynamic client registration)
passthrough.tokenHeld: Token held for this browser session. Tools can now be previewed and configured; the token was not saved to LiteLLM.

upstreamTokenHeader.label: Token Header (optional)
upstreamTokenHeader.tooltip: Which upstream header carries the token LiteLLM resolves for this server. Leave blank to send it as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>', which is the default and what most servers expect. Set a header name when the upstream expects it elsewhere, for example an API gateway that terminates its own credential on 'esb-oauth' while a separate Authorization from Static Headers passes through to the server behind it.

truePassthrough.title: True Passthrough disables LiteLLM authentication for this server
truePassthrough.description: Anyone who can reach the gateway can call this server without a LiteLLM key. The caller's Authorization header is forwarded to the upstream verbatim, per-key and per-team rate limits and spend tracking do not apply, and the upstream is fully responsible for authenticating callers. Choose OAuth Delegate instead if callers should still authenticate to LiteLLM.

permissions.title: Permission Management / Access Control
permissions.subtitle: Configure access permissions and security settings (Optional)
permissions.allowAllKeysTooltip: When enabled, every API key can access this MCP server.
permissions.allowAllKeysHint: Enable if this server should be "public" to all keys.
permissions.internalOnlyTooltip: When on, only requests from within your internal network are accepted. Turn off to allow external clients (other clusters, ChatGPT, etc). API key authentication is always required regardless of this setting.
permissions.internalOnlyHint: Turn on to restrict access to callers within your internal network only.
permissions.delegateAuthTooltip: When on, LiteLLM skips its own API key/SSO check for this server and lets the client complete PKCE directly with the upstream MCP server. Only honored when Auth Type is oauth2. No spend tracking or per-key rate limiting will run on this route.
permissions.delegateAuthHint: Bypass LiteLLM auth so clients authenticate directly with the upstream OAuth MCP server.
permissions.oauthPassthroughTooltip: When on, this server is treated as an OAuth pass-through: the gateway proxies the upstream /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource metadata, emits spec-compliant 401 challenges when no bearer is supplied, and propagates upstream 401/403 responses. Only honored when Auth Type is None and 'Authorization' is in Extra Headers.
permissions.oauthPassthroughHint: Forward upstream OAuth discovery and 401 challenges so clients negotiate OAuth directly with the upstream MCP server.
permissions.internalDelegateTitle: Internal server with upstream OAuth delegation
permissions.internalDelegateBody: This MCP server is configured as internal-only but delegates auth to upstream. Anonymous users will be able to reach the upstream OAuth2 /authorize flow without a LiteLLM session. Ensure your upstream provider and network enforce access controls.
permissions.accessGroupsTooltip: Specify access groups for this MCP server. Users must be in at least one of these groups to access the server.

permissions.extraHeadersTooltip: Forward custom headers from incoming requests to this MCP server (e.g., Authorization, X-Custom-Header, User-Agent)
permissions.staticHeadersTooltip: Send these key-value headers with every request to this MCP server.

toolSearch.alertDescription: Controls the mcp_tool_search virtual tool that native MCP clients call to discover tools. With an embedding model set, tools are ranked by the meaning of their name and description, so a query like "FX" finds a "foreign exchange rates" tool. Without one, keyword matching is used. Callers only ever see tools their key, team and server permissions already allow.

toolSearch.topKTooltip: Most ranked tools a search returns. A smaller top_k in the tool call wins. Core tools do not count.
toolSearch.thresholdTooltip: Lowest cosine similarity a tool needs to appear in semantic results. 0 means no cutoff.
toolSearch.alwaysFirstTooltip: One tool name per line, e.g. my_server-get_rates. Listed before ranked results whenever the caller is allowed to use them.
